source.title: Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Yi-Huai Hong; Yuelin Zou; Lijie Hu; Ziqian Zeng; Di Wang; Haiqin Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning-based unlearning changes access to targeted knowledge by restoring model activations or parameters, a different intervention from the simple attacks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports target-QA BLEU curves and discusses target-knowledge recovery across layer sweeps. The curves do not provide text-extractable values for each model, method, and epoch; the rows below capture explicit restoration results and the unrelated-QA capability impact. The patching study uses DPO and Gradient Difference; the global-impact experiment also uses NPO and NPO+KL.
record.test_reason: The study patches activations and restores parameters from the vanilla model into DPO- and Gradient Difference-unlearned LLaMA2-7B-chat and OLMo-7B, and shows target outputs return (KRS >0.9). This bears directly on C: unlearning blocks access rather than deleting. It also measures unrelated-QA degradation, which bears on the 'keeps general ability' part of A.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that fine-tuning unlearning leaves the knowledge in the MLP value vectors and changes how it is retrieved, mainly via final-layer MLP coefficients, with attention contributing partly through those coefficients. They find these methods vulnerable to recovery attacks on component activations and harmful to unrelated knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DPO and Gradient Difference for the patching investigation and DPO, NPO, NPO+KL, and Gradient Difference for global-impact tests; evaluates component restoration and QA BLEU rather than the original cited unlearning recipes as a recovery attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by component and layer: isolated coefficient restoration in the final layers is much stronger than value-vector restoration or isolated attention restoration. Unrelated QA BLEU declines with additional training epochs.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The KRS results are reported without uncertainty estimates. The global QA results are plotted without extractable per-method numeric values in the provided text. The study tests two models and selected concepts; it does not test chance-level target accuracy or the fine-tuning, quantization, and prompting attacks in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the explicit restoration outcomes. Method-specific target-QA BLEU values and the detailed per-layer curves in Figures 1–3 are not separately extracted where the provided text does not permit assigning values to a model, method, and condition.

untested.parts: Whether target accuracy reaches near chance (only target QA BLEU is reported, figure-only), and whether simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge.
Ablating a single activation direction. Recovery here uses oracle activations and parameters copied from the vanilla model.
Not tested: no prompting, jailbreak, language or in-context attack.

missing.what: Non-isolated attention-state restoration: average KRS exceeds 0.3 (from layer 15) and 0.4 (from layer 27).
Non-isolated coefficient restoration from layer 20 or 29 onward yields strong recovery.
Target QA BLEU falls over epochs for all four methods, showing apparent unlearning success (figure-only).

record.verdict_notes: The recovery 'attack' needs the vanilla model's activations or parameters; it is an oracle analysis, not a realistic attack. KRS measures closeness of logits (MSE) to the vanilla model over 30 tokens on 10 questions, not answer accuracy. Results are averaged over DPO and Gradient Difference with no per-method split and no uncertainty reported. The first author also wrote the ConceptVectors benchmark (arXiv:2406.11614), which supplies the concepts used here.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance, or test whether simple attacks fail to recover knowledge. It does report effects on unrelated QA performance.
No relearning attack using a small set of unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
It tests activation-state and component-parameter restoration, not ablation of a single activation direction.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
No robust counter-method is tested against the listed attacks.

rows.note: The authors state that the decline in unrelated QA BLEU indicates impact on unrelated behavior and capability; separate method-specific numeric values are not extractable from the provided figure.
rows.check: Version code V1 is invalid; link to A. The row measures retention of general ability, which A says should hold, and it does not hold: unrelated QA BLEU falls with training epochs. The baseline is the vanilla model's own responses, since BLEU compares outputs before and after unlearning, so it is effectively 1.0 at epoch 0. Values are figure-only. Authors say methods 'significantly impair' unrelated capabilities. 'Reversed' overstates a degradation.

relationships.condition: DPO and Gradient Difference unlearning on LLaMA2-7B-chat and OLMo-7B; restoring final-layer MLP coefficients, or coefficients plus attention states
relationships.reason: Restoring coefficients gives KRS ≥0.8 and joint restoration a peak >0.9 (r7–r10). Restoring value vectors recovers nothing (r3, r4), consistent with blocked access rather than deletion.
relationships.display_finding: Coefficient restoration yields KRS ≥0.8, adding attention-state restoration peaks above 0.9, and restoring value vectors alone recovers nothing.

relation.reason: Its own patching results bear on version C.

tranche.reason: It uses a different method (activation patching and parameter restoration from the vanilla model) on the same question: does unlearning block access or delete the knowledge?

source_check.notes: KRS is a logit-MSE recovery score over 30 generated tokens and 10 questions per concept, averaged over DPO and Gradient Difference, not accuracy. Section 3 uses a five-layer recovery window, while Appendix C isolates each component. Apart from the thresholds stated in the text, values come from figures only. Unrelated-QA BLEU compares outputs before and after unlearning, so it measures output drift rather than correctness.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Restoring coefficients recovers KRS to 0.8 or above in the final layers, and joint restoration has a peak above 0.9, consistent with unlearning obstructing access rather than fully deleting the knowledge (r7–r10).
